gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power the stations draw with the AC outlets switched on and nothing plugged in. The Solar Lab measured about 13.8 W on the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, ChatGPT's 'best all-around' pick. Techtest.org measured about 2.5–2.8 W on the 230 V EU Anker SOLIX S2000. Leaving the inverter on for a 10-hour night therefore costs the C1000 Gen 2 about 138 Wh, roughly 16% of the 890 Wh OutdoorGearLab measured from it.
standout_why: The two cited pages have no measurements at all. yourpowersetup.com shows only maker specs and leaves out the S2000. greenmachineadventures.com says it is 'not a claim that Amy and Ryan personally lab-tested every model' and repeats maker recharge times. Of the top results I opened, outagereadyhq.com (camping best list) says it uses vendor documentation only, assumes 85% usable and calls the Anker 'quietest on paper at 20 dB'. solarpowerauditor.com (rank 10, not cited) does have bench figures: C1000 Gen 2 884 Wh, 52 minutes and 52 dBA at full output; Explorer 1000 v2 905 Wh. So usable capacity and Anker noise are partly covered already, but it has no Plus-specific figures and no AC-on idle draw for any model. The TechRadar page came back truncated. unpluggedwatts.com could not be opened (SSL error).
decides: This mostly confirms ChatGPT's picks but adds one caveat. The measured usable energy of the ~1 kWh units is close: 890 Wh for the C1000 Gen 2 and 910 Wh for the Explorer 1000 v2 (OutdoorGearLab), and 910 Wh for the DELTA 3 Plus (StorageReview). That supports ChatGPT's 85% runtime assumption. For overnight camping with an AC-powered device left on, the C1000 Gen 2's ~13.8 W idle draw and its fan noise at high load hurt it. Notebookcheck measured about 45 dB at 1 m under high load, OutdoorGearLab called the fan 'frustratingly loud', and OutdoorGearLab said the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2's fans 'stayed nearly silent'. For quiet nights, that favours the Jackery or the S2000 (which idled at ~2.5–2.8 W in techtest's EU test). Treat it as a strong pointer, not proof: the C1000 and S2000 idle figures come from different labs and different-voltage versions.
